newsitem.title: USA: Calif. offers reward in probe of fire that killed 9.
newsitem.headline: Calif. offers reward in probe of fire that killed 9.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson offered a $50,000 reward Monday to help investigators find those responsible for an arson fire that swept through a house in April, killing nine people.

Wilson signed a proclamation offering the reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the person or persons who set the fire. Detectives said they have yet to identify any suspects.

Five children, aged 5 to 11, and four women, all from the same family, died in the early-morning fire April 26 in East Palo Alto, 50 miles south of San Francisco. A flammable substance was found in the carport where investigators believe the fire started, detectives said.

"Those who committed this cowardly act must be brought to justice," Wilson, a Republican, said in a statement. "The state must do everything within its power to catch the criminal or criminals who are responsible."
The victims were trapped inside the house by burglar bars bolted on the windows, a common window feature of the neighbourhood, which has a high crime rate.
Firefighters had a hard time getting into the building because a burning car blocked access to the front door and two angry pit bulls barred their way when they tried to go to the back of the house.
Menlo Park Fire District Chief Rick Tye said it was the deadliest fire in the district's 80-year history.
